shared_object_grammar.purpose: Project Shopping through the same OBJECT → FOCUS → OPERATION → RETURN grammar without mutating the native detailed lifecycle.

object.need: NEED is a desired-state object, not a product. FIND creates/links a THING candidate through MAY_BE_SATISFIED_BY.
object.thing: THING is one exact candidate/owned material object with identity, promise, native lifecycle, evidence, fit, cost and burden.
object.law: NEED != THING; projection may relate them but must not collapse aspiration into product identity.

focus.law: One exact object + one current question. FIT, COST, BURDEN and PROOF remain unequal evidence lenses rather than new object identities.

operations.authority: Shared verbs HOLD/TURN/RELEASE/TRACE/RETURN are projections only. Native Shopping/HOUSE/Dayline/human authority remains unchanged.

return.law: External hosts may return evidence only. Shopping revalidates exact item identity + native lifecycle before accepting a receipt; RETURN cannot silently purchase, install, receive or adopt.

readiness.rule: READY is derived, not manually asserted.
readiness.minimum: existing purchase gate passes and required external evidence is not stale/unknown
readiness.caveat: Domain-specific gates may add FIT/compatibility/risk requirements; projection must fail closed when required evidence is absent.

adoption.rule: TESTED is evidence under ON_HAND; ADOPTED requires the named adoption criterion.
adoption.ownership_boundary: After ADOPTED, the material object may participate in shared FIELD/HOUSE inventory while Shopping retains procurement provenance rather than owning all future maintenance state.

residue.law: Compression may reduce visible lifecycle states only when every suppressed distinction remains inspectable and round-trippable.

promotion_gate: implement as a projection over existing browser-local v0.1 ledger; no destructive migration
prove legacy import/export bytes retain native states
